text:
maria_cs: Quick preflight for Vega Labs dedicated bring-up tomorrow 09:00 PT. Need final quota plan, autoscale thresholds, and a short demo script for their SREs. Who can take ownership of the traffic profile + warmup steps?

jamie_se: I can own the demo script. Will draft a run that covers cold-cache, warm-cache, and a sustained 300 qps spike.

liam_ops: I will handle the autoscale thresholds and infra knobs. Which instance types are we pinning for the reserved pool?

maria_cs: Vega is on a 32-GPU reserved pool (A100 40GB equiv). They requested predictable p95 latency <= 180ms and an initial quota of 250 qps, burst to 400 qps for 10m.

jamie_se: Got it. Draft outline: 1) Health checks + readiness probe, 2) Cold priming (10m @ 50 qps), 3) Warmup cache sweep (5m @ 150 qps), 4) Spike (10m @ 350 qps), 5) Steady-state soak (30m @ 200 qps). Will include short curl checks for validation.

liam_ops: For autoscale: set lower bound pool=4 pods, upper bound=16, scale-up at 70% GPU mem or sustained queue length > 80 for 60s, scale-down below 40% for 5m. Also enable emergency fallback to smaller quantized model if p95 > 300ms for >2m.

neal_poc: Vega ops here — that sound reasonable. Question: does warmup do prefix caching or KV priming? We saw cold token gen really spike latencies last time.

jamie_se: We'll run KV priming via a short synthetic prefix set. Example command I plan to include:```bash
loadgen --endpoint https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate --qps 150 --duration 300 --model "vega-served-v1" --seed-prefix-file warm_prefixes.txt
```
This primes KV/cache and hits the stateful paths.

maria_cs: Perfect. Also need someone to run the quota throttle verification — confirm token accounting and throttles won't cut the bake. Liam?

liam_ops: I'll run the quota smoke with the billing team. Quick script for smoke check: ```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.test/v1/health || echo 'down'
# then fire 5 concurrent gen requests and check 200s
```
I'll post results to the runbook channel before 08:30 PT.

deploy-bot: image-redwood/vega:2026-03-22 promoted to staging. Link: https://ci.redwood/build/vega/4521 :rocket:

jamie_se: Small note — can we pin the model variant for the canary? Use ve-ga-vcrt-q8 to simulate quantized fallback during the spike test. Adds realism for recovery checks.

liam_ops: Agree. Canary policy: 10% traffic to canary variant for first 5m, then 30% if stable. Fallback automated after 2 consecutive 5m windows of >5% errors or p95 breach.

neal_poc: We can join the test window. One ask: can you include a short checklist for our on-call so they know the exact metrics to watch?

maria_cs: Yes — I'll produce a 1-page ops checklist: health endpoints, key dashboards (latency p50/p95/p99, GPU mem, queue length), rollback steps, contact list. Will post by EOD.

jamie_se: Adding demo script bullets for the Vega SREs (will paste into the doc): 1) run KV priming, 2) run cold-cache job, 3) observe latency jump, 4) kick spike, 5) validate fallback and rollback.

liam_ops: I'll add autoscale graphs and thresholds to the dashboard. Also I'll pre-create an alert that fires if p95 > 220ms for 3m.

neal_poc: Thanks all — we'll be ready. Can you send the final runbook link and the exact test window (we have a maintenance freeze at 10:30 PT)?

maria_cs: Final window: 09:00-10:15 PT. No changes after 10:00 (dry-run buffer). Runbook link will be posted here by 20:00 PT (internal doc). :thumbsup:

jamie_se: Draft runbook uploaded: https://docs.redwood/vega/onboard-runbook (internal). Includes scripts and the curl commands.

liam_ops: Quota smoke complete — no unexpected throttles. Posting logs to the doc. All set from infra side.

neal_poc: Received — thanks team. See you at 09:00 PT.
